title: Prowe
headline: Legal software that runs on your own server.
intro: Prowe is a modular platform for law firms and legal departments. It covers documents, matters, outside counsel evaluation and contract analysis. Every module runs on a shared core that handles accounts, permissions and the audit log.
description: Prowe is a modular platform for law firms and legal departments that runs on your own server.

goals.title: Your data stays with you
goals.text: Prowe is installed on your organization's own server. Client files stay out of someone else's cloud unless an administrator connects an outside service, such as a database or an AI model.

goals.title: History you can audit
goals.text: The audit log is append-only: the application has no permission to change it. In Galena, every version of a document is kept, along with who made it and when.

goals.title: One platform
goals.text: One account and one sign-in for every available module. Accounts and module access live in one admin panel.

goals.title: Open foundations
goals.text: Prowe is built on open-source software, mostly under permissive licenses. Data lives in a PostgreSQL database, Git repositories and ordinary files, not in a closed format.

goals.title: Polish and English
goals.text: Interface in Polish and English. In Sygna, the English version covers only the main labels for now.

modules.name: Atrium
modules.summary: The front door: launcher, module catalog and administration.
modules.body:
Atrium shows the modules you have access to and lets you request the rest. Administrators manage accounts and access to every module from it.

- A launcher with your modules and a module switcher in the top bar
- A module catalog with access requests
- Access for people and organizational units, including the units below them
- Accounts, module access and the organizational structure in one place, with its own audit log

modules.name: Galena
modules.summary: A shared drive for your team, with the full history of every change.
modules.body:
Galena looks like an ordinary drive: workspaces, folders, moving files by drag-and-drop, sharing. Underneath, every file lives in a Git repository, so the change history records itself and nobody needs to know Git.

- History of every file: who changed what, and when
- An interactive graph of all versions
- Optional review: drafts with comment threads and approval before publishing
- PDF and image preview
- Optional encryption of individual files (AES-256-GCM)

modules.name: Sygna
modules.summary: Practice management: clients, matters, deadlines and time recording.
modules.body:
With Sygna you run a matter from first contact with the client to billing.

- Clients, matters and the parties to them
- Conflict-of-interest check when a matter is opened
- Procedural deadlines and time recording
- Information barriers: named people, administrators included, lose access to a walled matter

modules.name: Counsel Scorecard
modules.summary: Outside counsel evaluation: scored questionnaires with a full answer history.
modules.body:
Counsel Scorecard is for building scored questionnaires. Out of the box, a legal department uses it to rate its outside law firms, and the answers are kept together with their change history.

- Questions, answer options and a weight for each question
- Scores calculated automatically
- Every correction to an answer stays in the history
- Full-text search that shows only what you have access to

modules.name: Compass
modules.summary: Contract analysis with a lawyer's sign-off on the report.
modules.body:
Compass helps law firms and legal departments analyze contracts. A lawyer runs the analysis, reads the report and signs off that they have reviewed it.

- A contract card: parties, term, renewal and whether the contract is in force, each value backed by a quote from the contract
- The firm's red lines (e.g. a cap on contractual penalties): a verdict on every rule, pointing to the clause
- The AI model runs locally, e.g. on the lawyer's laptop, or at an outside provider the administrator picks (EU/EEA only by default)

stack.label: Database
stack.value: PostgreSQL; a separate schema and roles for each module

stack.label: Deployment
stack.value: Docker Compose and Caddy on a single server
